questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in an English-speaking country. Australia not only offers well-respected universities but is also a travel destination that can be difficult to visit independently, given the significant distance and costs involved in traveling from Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a fantastic time overall

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: it was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not need any assistance upon arrival, as everything was completed prior to arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I did not need any assitance upon arrival, so I cant answer this. However, it was my perception that the orientation and assistance available at UNSW was good.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was okay, be aware that it is very expensive to live in Sydney, especially in the popular areas (semi) close to the University, e.g. Bondi, Cooge, Paddington, CBD, Surry Hills etc. Be prepared to spend a lot of time upon arrival looking for housing, as many of the options are really bad.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Finding quality housing in Sydney is both expensive and time consuming, so be prepared to invest significant time in your search. Beyond options like Scape or Iglu (very expensive btw), I highly recommend joining Facebook groups such as 'Young Danes in Sydney' or using platforms like
Flatmates.com.au
. Crucially, unless you use Scape or Iglu, never transfer money before arriving in Sydney and inspecting the property in person. Scams are common, and seeing the place first is the only way to ensure it's legitimate and worthwhile.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: See the answers above.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Course registration at UNSW was a complete mess. The support for exchange students was unhelpful and often provided wrong and useless information. I spent countless hours applying for courses that were rejected without cause, only to have them approved later after a tedious dispute process. Sometimes, they just rejected the course with the explanation "course prerequisites not met", despite the course having no prerequisites. It was infuriating.  
To make matters worse, all of this work was useless, as UNSW sent a 'final' list of courses available to exchange students around 45 days before semester start. This meant that all the headaches associated with my initial course registration was completely meaningless because the courses i applied for and got accepted to were not even offered to exchange students.

For future exchange students, I recommend not stressing over course registration. 90% of the courses you find on their website will not be available for exchange students, so dont waste too much time on course registration.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Apart from course registration, the registration process was easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mail correspondance from people at UNSW, who were not very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end, we got a 'final list' of courses available to exchange students. From this list, I got everything that i registered for, but there were not too many courses to choose from.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not spent too much time on it. Await communication from UNSW on e-mail follow the steps there. It will also be possible to swap courses in the beginning of the semester, so no need to worry too much about courses.  Wait for the final list of courses that exchange students can register for. Dont waste your precious time, like I and others did!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was definately easier than at UCPH. Be aware, that group exams can be common in some courses; additionally, UNSW has many Chinese students, who speak (very) limited English, which can be a bit tedious, especially in group work and group assignments.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Pretty easy to be honest.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is more group work and a higher level of interaction between teachers and students at UNSW compared to UCPH. Additionally, grades are not determined by a single final exam; instead, they are weighted across various assignments that must be completed throughout the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: The Australian Legal System in a Comparative Perspective, International Relations and Sport, Legal Project Management, Introduction to Chinese Regulation of International Business.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Overall, the courses were quite interesting. I particularly enjoyed my first three subjects and would highly recommend Legal Project Management. While most of the courses were relatively easy to pass, the Chinese Regulation course was not the best course, additionally, it required a 6,000-word individual assignment worth 60% of the final grade, which felt disproportionate for a 6 UoC/7,5 ECTS course.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Visa 7000 DKK, plane tickets for 11.000 DKK, Australian health insurance (mandatory) - 1.500 DKK. 

I don't recall the amount I spent per month on food, personal expenses and other fees, so the figures provided above are a bit inaccurate. I also spent heavily on travel, social experiences, eating out etc., so my numbers shouldn't be taken as a standard baseline. 

I finished the semester at the end of November, but keep in mind that I stayed for an additional two months having fun in Sydney and travelling a lot.
 
In total, expect to pay around 90.000 +/- DKK in total for 5 months in Sydney with costs being higher depending on the ammount of travel, social experiences, duration of your stay etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was cheaper than Denmark, housing was more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They offered a lot of opportunities, but i did not use them a lot. I would recommend to try some of them. I played tennis, which was fun.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All types of sports activities, parties etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surfing or other sports you are interested in picking up.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going to the beaches and enjoying happy hours at different pubs and bars. Travel to other places in Australia, such as the East and West Coast. Also, I highly recommend going on a surf camp, it was a great experience! Watch out for events in Sydney, there is a lot happening all the time, especially in Spring and Summer time.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, Australians are very nice and fun people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be friendly.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Australians are very calm and down to earth.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Just enjoy your time! It will be an unforgetable experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont worry, things will work out, especially everything regarding course registration.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of great people and travelling around in Australia.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being far away from friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Make the most of your exchange semester. Say yes to new experiences, stay open-minded, and embrace the chance to meet people from all over the world. Your exchange is what you make of it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
